results.evidence: The itinerary's 4,400 ft to the Bench and '~5,800 ft one-way' are impossible against the row's own pins (pullout 4,300, creek 4,080, Bench 6,460, summit 8,203), but no outside source states a car-to-car gain for Ares Tower. One source states ~4,400 ft from the highway to Burgundy Col (itself more than the 4,300->7,800 ft difference), another gives 2,500 ft trailhead-to-col; neither is a figure for this route, and the rules forbid computing gain_ft from pin arithmetic.

Two sources put Burgundy Col about 3 mi from the SR-20 pullout (matching the col pin's distMi 3), and Ares Tower lies north of the col along the ridge, so the one-way distance is roughly 3.5 mi; but no source states the one-way figure to Ares Tower itself. dist_km 11.27 renders as a 7.0 mi ONE-WAY approach and agrees with totalNote's '~7 mi one-way', both likely a round-trip number, and the itinerary day miles (3.3 + 7) disagree with the pins. Without a sourced one-way figure to the summit, dist_km and the itinerary are left unchanged.

results.evidence: The only dissenting copy is bivy[0].permit on the shared regional Bench Camp entry, which is owned by the separate camping clean-up; no bivy patch is written. The Bench Camp entry does serve this route (it names Vasiliki Ridge as its main use); the hidden 'The Bench' row is a duplicate of it.

The first-ascent account calls the route 'a two- or three-pitch, well protected climb (5.9)', with pitch grades 5.7, 5.8+, 5.9 and 5.7. No second outside source describes this line; rock_grade, overview and every pitch grade in beta already say 5.9, so the lone 5.10 in `grade` is corrected (grade_num is derived and not patched).

The first-ascent account describes a first and second pitch in detail and calls the route two- or three-pitch; the beta on this row describes the same two pitches. A pitch count of 0 is impossible; 2 is the number of pitches actually described.

7,663 ft is wrong: the route climbs 240 ft (2 pitches, per the route listing) from Burgundy Col, which sources put at ~7,800 ft. But the replacement cannot be settled: one topo-derived list gives Vasiliki Tower 7,940 ft, a trip-report site 7,920 ft, and USGS 1 m lidar sampled just north of the col returns a local high of ~8,060 ft over a ~7,830 ft saddle, which also fits col + 240 ft. The sources disagree by more than 100 ft, so high_point_ft is left for a ground-based pass.

The route listing gives the South Face as 3 pitches, 250 ft, 5.6, Grade II, which matches pitches=3 and length_m 76. The overview, beta and ROUTE BREAKDOWN say two pitches, but the ROUTE BREAKDOWN text (face to a sandy bench, then a slab with a finger crack on the left) is the Northwest Face's description, so the two-pitch prose looks copied from the neighbouring route. Only one source gives a count, so nothing is changed.

results.evidence: Summit: 7,663 ft (on high_point_ft and the summit pin) is below the col and wrong, but the sources disagree (topo list 7,940 ft, trip-report site 7,920 ft, USGS lidar ~8,060 ft local high just north of the col), so it is left unresolved. The col half of this contradiction is settled separately (see the discovered Burgundy Col entry).

SummitPost describes '7800-foot Burgundy Col'; the Northwest Face route listing and the club route page both put camps at Burgundy Col (7,800 ft); USGS lidar gives the saddle just south of Vasiliki Tower at ~7,830 ft. One trip-report site says 7,720 ft. The row's itinerary already says ~7,800 ft; the col pin (7,950) and the approach text (~7,720) are brought into line.
